clue.text: Orders mother employs going after husband?

indicators.note: going after says the following words come later in the answer than the word that comes before them

parts.note: man is an old word for husband, as in man and wife
a dam is an animal's mother
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A household where mother takes over and starts giving the orders once the husband has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the husband last, but he comes first in the answer: mother-and-employs goes after him.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandamus is a writ from a higher court commanding a lower body to act, so the plural means legal orders.

clue.text: Fly I had found under nasty scum

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece found under another is written below it, so it comes later
something nasty is in a bad state, so the word after it is spoilt into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone finds an insect lying beneath a layer of foul scum.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscid is any insect of the housefly family Muscidae.

clue.text: Unhealthy lumps of nasty nature covering old mother

indicators.note: to cover something here is to wrap around it, so one piece goes round the other
nasty suggests something gone bad, so the word that follows is spoilt into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
O is the standard abbreviation for old
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A grim medical finding: growths of a nasty kind spreading over an elderly mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' reads as describing the lumps, but it is the signal that nature is to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuromata (plural of neuroma) are tumours of nerve tissue, the unhealthy lumps of the definition.

clue.text: Hint of cold in European spring

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a Dane is a European, from Denmark

indicators.note: a hint is only a trace of the whole, so just the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of cold

explanation.surface: A weather note: a touch of chill in a European springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring looks like the season but is the verb; C goes inside DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to leap, and dance can mean to leap or skip about lightly.

clue.text: Inspection of cloth, a product one put out with silver lining

indicators.note: a lining sits on the inside, so the metal goes within the other letters
putting one out means the letter I, standing for one, is thrown out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
a line is a range of goods a firm sells
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A cloth inspector notes a manufactured item released with a silver lining.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the I (one) from LINE to leave LNE, then line it with AG: A + LN(AG)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Alnage was the official measurement and inspection of woollen cloth, done by an alnager for the Crown.

clue.text: Conservative group of theologians in order upset one of mixed race

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the whole build reads from the bottom
in sets one group of letters inside the other

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the ulema are the body of Muslim religious scholars

explanation.surface: A Tory faction of theologians is thrown into disarray within a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: The ulema are Islamic scholars, not a Christian body; OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Brazil a mameluco is a person of mixed European and Indigenous descent.

clue.text: Saving scheme for African people

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rotating savings club, as in West Africa and the Caribbean
second meaning: a people of Guinea and Sierra Leone

explanation.surface: A savings plan set up for people in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The same short word names an informal pooled-savings club and an ethnic group of West Africa.

clue.text: Stop having water to flush away a pesticide

indicators.note: having means the first word holds the next one alongside it, so they sit together

parts.note: to stop is to end

indicators.note: flushing something away removes it, here the letter written as the word a

parts.note: rain is falling water
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone stops using water to flush a pesticide away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' looks like the article before the definition, but it is the letter flushed out of RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Endrin is an organochlorine insecticide, now banned in most countries.

clue.text: Female domination at home with the introduction of a German governess?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: introducing something means bringing it inside, so the letter goes into the word for domination

parts.note: rule is power or domination
taken as written
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A household where a German governess arrives and the women take control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With the introduction of' reads as the governess arriving, but it puts the lone letter inside the word for domination.
explanation.definitionFit: Fräulein, German for a young unmarried woman, was used in English for a German governess; the question mark flags the narrower sense.

clue.text: Part of waterway, say, with weak pillar erected on it

indicators.note: in a down entry, on it puts this piece on top of the rest
in a down entry, something erected is stood upright, so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a lat is a Buddhist monumental pillar in India
W is the abbreviation for weak
e.g. means for example, which say can mean

explanation.surface: A canal engineer raises a weak pillar beside a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: LAT is flipped and set above W and EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A talweg (thalweg) is the line of deepest flow along a river or valley, so part of a waterway.

clue.text: Compound in waste liquid's imagined to be lacking nitrogen

definitions.note: a possessive standing for the adjective 'of urea'

indicators.note: lacking means something is missing, so the letter named after it is taken out

parts.note: something imagined is unreal
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemist decides a compound found in urine was merely imagined, since it contains no nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: Urea is the compound in urine; the possessive 's turns it into 'urea's', which the adjective means.
explanation.definitionFit: Ureal is the adjective meaning of or relating to urea, the nitrogenous compound excreted in urine.

clue.text: Tree beginning to shrivel on icy area with temperature dropping

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of shrivel

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: tundra is the frozen treeless plain of the Arctic
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A tree starts to shrivel on frozen ground as the temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: S then TUNDRA without its T.
explanation.definitionFit: The sundra (sundari) is an Indian mangrove tree of the Sundarbans, valued for its hard timber.

clue.text: Resist SM's order on parade ground

definitions.meaning: first meaning: avoid or keep away from
second meaning: the clipped drill command for attention barked by a sergeant major

explanation.walkthrough: SM is a sergeant major; his shout of 'Attention!' on parade comes out as a single clipped syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Shun means avoid, and 'Shun! is the shortened form of the drill order attention.

clue.text: What could make maiden pine is being trapped — heart going astray?

indicators.note: something trapped is caught inside, so this short word sits within the other letters

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A lovelorn maiden pining with a wandering heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart is a card suit, not an organ: a heart going to the wrong player happens when cards are dealt wrongly. Deal is pine timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeal is a wrong distribution of cards, so a heart might end up in the wrong hand.

clue.text: Nightshade plants in the region of flowing water

parts.note: circa means about or around
ea is a dialect word for a river or running water

explanation.surface: Nightshade growing near a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Circaea is the genus of enchanter's nightshade, plants of damp woods named after the sorceress Circe.

clue.text: Join up together in international entrance to the south of Scottish island

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece to the south is written beneath, so it follows the other

parts.note: Coll is an island of the Inner Hebrides
I is the abbreviation for international
a gate is an entrance

explanation.walkthrough: COLL is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To colligate is to bind or link things together, from Latin colligare.

clue.text: Birds of a similar nature isle's accommodating

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man, with the possessive S
akin means similar

explanation.walkthrough: The isle is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea; its possessive S closes the word around the similar-nature piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Manakins are small brightly coloured birds of tropical American forests.

clue.text: I'll be blooming pleased — I love the French

parts.note: glad means pleased
I as written, then love as zero in tennis, written O
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An exclamation: 'I'll be blooming pleased — I love the French!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British oath, but in the definition it means flowering: the speaker is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiole is a gladiolus, a flowering plant, so it can say it will be in bloom.

clue.text: A head twitching and merging in with the background

parts.note: taken as written
a pate is the head
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A twitching head that blends into the background, like a nervous creature hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Apatetic describes animal colouring that camouflages it against its surroundings.

clue.text: Expletive restrained, curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means its tail is cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a river that is dammed is held back, restrained

explanation.surface: A swear word held back and cut short, as if bitten off mid-oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Damme, short for damn me, is an old oath or exclamation.

clue.text: Leaping around? You could do without a ___!

definitions.text: Leaping around? You could do without a ___!

indicators.note: around suggests moving about, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
without here means lacking, so the single letter written as a is dropped from the word

parts.note: the word to be reduced and rearranged
the letter removed

explanation.surface: A wry aside: you could manage leaping about without one of these.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a man with a wooden leg will hardly go leaping about.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin leg is a wooden leg, which would make leaping around hard to manage.

clue.text: Certain to look untidy with hair finally neglected, growing out?

indicators.note: untidy suggests disorder, so the letters are jumbled
something neglected is left out, so that letter is dropped

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of hair

explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing out' seems part of the hair story but is the definition, with a question mark for its rarity.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives enate and enatic as growing out, a botanical term for outgrowths.

clue.text: Old turtles here will have moseyed around

indicators.note: around suggests moving things about, so the letters are rearranged
the answer with the extra letter added will have the longer word's letters, so that letter is taken away first

parts.note: the longer word the letters come from
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Old turtles that have wandered slowly about this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus O (old) rearranges to MOSEYED. 'Here' points at the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Emydes is the old plural of emys, a freshwater tortoise or terrapin.

clue.text: One involved in bomb-making is an informer
